'''Shalby Hospitals''' is a multispecialty hospital with facilities in various locations. The hospital was first started in [[Ahmedabad]] as a [[joint replacement]] centre in 1994 by [[Vikram I. Shah|Dr. Vikram Shah]].<ref name="fdate" /> Shalby today, runs a chain of 14 multispecialty hospitals in [[Ahmedabad]], [[Rajkot]], [[Surat]], [[Vapi]], [[Indore]], [[Gwalior]], [[Jabalpur]], [[Jaipur]], [[Lucknow]], [[Ranchi]] and [[Mohali]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Contact Shalby Hospitals in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, India |url=https://www.shalby.org/contact-us/ |access-date=2022-05-08 |language=en}}</ref>

==History==
The hospital, located in [[Ahmedabad]], was established in 1994 by Dr. Vikram Shah as a small six-bedded single specialty unit that offered total knee replacement (TKR) surgery.<ref name="FE March 2010">{{cite web|url=http://archivehealthcare.expressbpd.com/201003/strategy01.shtml|title=Healing with Compassion|last=Shukla|first=Sonal |date=March 2010|publisher=[[The Financial Express (India)|Financial Express]]|accessdate=4 January 2017}}</ref>

== Shalby Hospital ==
By 2007, it had become a 200-bed multispecialty hospital. It includes 40 medical disciplines ranging from [[cardiology]], [[cardiothoracic surgery]], [[Oral Surgery|dental care]], [[oncology]] and [[Trauma surgery|trauma]] to [[Otorhinolaryngology|ENT]].<ref name="FE March 2010" /><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.timescontent.com/syndication-photos/reprint/feature/276033/shalby-hospital-ahmedabad-health-gu.html|title=Shalby Hospital|last=|first=|date=|website=|publisher=Times Content|access-date=}}</ref>

In 2011, it acquired a 55 percent stake in the Vrundavan Hospital in Goa, which had 120 beds across two units.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.thehindubusinessline.com/todays-paper/tp-others/tp-states/shalby-acquires-55-stake-in-goa-hospital-to-set-up-new-ones-in-gujarat/article2440367.ece|title=Shalby acquires 55% stake in Goa hospital; to set up new ones in Gujarat|last=|first=|website=|publisher=[[The Hindu]] Business Line |date=9 September 2011 |accessdate=9 January 2016}}</ref> In 2012, Shalby acquired Krishna Hospital for an estimated Rs 75 crore, to become the biggest private corporate hospital in Ahmedabad.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/ahmedabad/Shalby-buys-Krishna-Hospital-for-Rs-75-crore/articleshow/16858149.cms |title=Shalby buys Krishna Hospital for Rs 75 crore |first=Radha |last=Sharma |work=Times of India |date=18 October 2012 |accessdate=9 January 2017}}</ref> By 2012 the company had 450 beds in Ahmedabad.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.business-standard.com/article/finance/hospital-chain-shalby-mulls-taking-pe-route-112102500658_1.html |title=Hospital chain Shalby mulls taking PE route |first=Soni |last=Das |work=[[Business Standard]] |date=25 October 2012 |accessdate=18 January 2017}}</ref>

In 2013, Shah claimed the hospital in Ahmedabad and completed an average of 30 joint replacement surgeries a day, at which point they had 705 employees.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.businesstoday.in/magazine/special/shalby-ltd-awarded-for-star-sme-services-2013/story/193876.html|title=Scalpel and Suit|last=Seetharaman|first=G.|date=28 April 2013|publisher=Business Today|accessdate=3 January 2016}}</ref>

During the period 1994–2009, the joint replacement team performed more than 20,000 TKR procedures.<ref name="FE March 2010" /> The length of surgical time in the hospital had been dramatically reduced from 1 hour and 20 mins per TKR to around 10 to 12 minutes<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|url=http://gulfnews.com/news/uae/health/the-10-minute-knee-replacement-surgery-in-the-uae-1.1447213|title=The 10-minute knee replacement surgery in the UAE|author=Suchitra Bajpai Chaudhary, Senior|date=26 January 2015|newspaper=Gulf News|access-date=9 January 2017}}</ref> using the "ZERO Technique" invented by Dr. Vikram Shah.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.indiamedicaltimes.com/2012/02/22/dr-vikram-shah-revolutionises-%E2%80%98total-knee-replacement%E2%80%99-surgery-with-%E2%80%98zero-technique%E2%80%99/|title=Dr Vikram Shah 'revolutionises' total knee replacement surgery with 'zero technique'|last=|first=|date=|website=|publisher=India Medical Times|access-date=}}</ref> Over the years, Shalby has performed over 1,00,000 Joint Replacement Surgeries.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.freepressjournal.in/indore/shalby-hospital-set-to-launch-state-of-the-art-cancer-care-unit/974952 |title=Shalby hospital set to launch state-of-the-art cancer care unit |work=[[The Free Press Journal]] |date=20 November 2016 |accessdate=18 January 2017}}</ref>

In 2011, Shalby received the Diplomat in National Board (DNB) certificate in Orthopaedics. At the time, it was the only hospital in [[Gujarat]] to have this.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dnaindia.com/india/report-shalby-hospital-gets-accreditation-in-orthopaedics-1489271|title=Shalby Hospital gets accreditation in orthopaedics|last=|first=|publisher=DNA India|date=2 January 2011|accessdate=9 January 2017}}</ref>
